name: Yankari National Park
blurb: Nigeria's most visited game reserve — warm-spring bathing at Wikki, elephants, baboons, and open savanna game drives.
activity: Game drives, warm-spring swimming, guided walks

name: Gashaka-Gumti National Park
blurb: Nigeria's largest park — misty highlands, chimpanzee populations, and the country's most demanding trekking terrain.

name: Cross River National Park
blurb: Rainforest canopy and one of the last strongholds of the Cross River gorilla, split across the Okwangwo and Oban divisions.

name: Obudu Mountain Resort
blurb: A cable-car ride onto the Obudu Plateau, with cool highland air, waterfalls, and views into Cameroon.
activity: Cable car, plateau hiking, highland cabins

name: Kainji Lake National Park
blurb: Nigeria's oldest national park, built around the Kainji reservoir, with the Borgu game reserve's giraffe and buffalo herds.
activity: Game viewing, boat trips on the lake

name: Old Oyo National Park
blurb: Savanna parkland layered over the ruins of the old Oyo Empire capital — wildlife and archaeology in the same reserve.

name: Chad Basin National Park
blurb: Semi-arid Sahel terrain around the shrinking Lake Chad basin, home to migratory birds and the Sambisa game reserve sector.

name: Kamuku National Park
blurb: Guinea savanna woodland on the Kaduna–Niger border, quieter and less visited than Nigeria's larger parks.

name: Okomu National Park
blurb: Lowland rainforest sheltering forest elephants and the white-throated monkey, with a well-used canopy walkway.

name: Lekki Conservation Centre
blurb: A protected wetland inside the city, crossed by West Africa's longest canopy walkway, minutes from Lekki's beaches.
activity: Canopy walkway, nature trail, picnic grounds

name: Millennium Park
blurb: Abuja's largest public park, split into two landscaped halves by the airport road, with fountains and open lawns.

name: Nike Lake Resort Park
blurb: A landscaped lakeside resort park on Enugu's edge, built around a natural lake framed by hills.

name: Isaac Boro Garden Park
blurb: A central Port Harcourt green space named for the Niger Delta activist, popular for evening walks and open-air events.
activity: Evening walks, open-air events, food stalls

name: Freedom Park
blurb: A former colonial-era prison on Lagos Island, converted into an open-air cultural and performance venue.
activity: Live music, cultural events, museum corner
